headline: Strong US payrolls end a four-day KTB rally and hike bets hold the front end: the 3Y rises 2.6bp to 3.639%, the 10Y only 1.0bp to 3.863% as a failed KOSPI rebound caps the long end, and 2s3s flattens to a 1-year low of 1bp
summary: KTBs weakened for the first time in five sessions in a bear flattener: the 2Y rose 2.8bp to 3.629% and the 3Y 2.6bp to 3.639% (64bp over the 3.00% base rate), against +1.0bp for the 10Y (3.863%) and +0.6bp for the 30Y (3.977%). 3s10s flattened 1.6bp to 22.4bp, back near Thursday's 1-year low of 21.8bp, and 2s3s is 1.0bp, its flattest of the year; month to date the 10Y is still −14.5bp and the 3Y −7.6bp. The money market kept tightening: CD rose 2bp to 3.36%, a 1-year high, CP held at 3.83% and MSB 91-day at 3.176% (96th percentile). Spread products barely moved: KDB 3Y 23bp over KTB (+0.9bp), AAA bank 1Y 43bp (93rd percentile), AA- 3Y 69bp (87th) and KEPCO 3Y 44bp, still near its 1-year wide.
drivers: US payrolls: Treasuries give back part of the rally

After Friday's KTB close the US added 165k jobs in October (65k expected, September revised up to 60k) and unemployment fell to 4.1%; December Fed hike odds rose to about 78% and the US 10Y par yield closed 2bp higher at 4.86% (2Y about +6bp). At the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 that implies +0.9bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual +1.0bp, so the 10Y move was essentially all global, but it explains only about a third of the 3Y's +2.6bp. The KTB–UST 10Y gap is −99.7bp, a fresh 1-year extreme; Treasuries were flat in Asia ahead of Monday's USD 58bn 3Y auction.
Hike pricing leads the front end

NH Investment and Citi both kept a November 26 hike to 3.25% as the base case despite last week's equity crash (Citi sees the cycle ending there if chip prices turn), and the bill curve agrees: CD rose 2bp to 3.36%, its highest in almost two years, CP 3.83% and MSB 91-day 3.176% are at 1-year highs, and CP–CD is 47bp (94th percentile). With the 3Y only 14bp above a 3.50% terminal, dealers cited level fatigue after 5–7-month lows, so the 1–3Y sector underperformed: 1s2s widened 1.1bp to 6.1bp while 2s3s fell to 1.0bp.
A failed KOSPI rebound caps the long end

KOSPI rallied as much as 2% to 5,172.94 on firmer US chips, then reversed to close −0.81% at 5,018.85, its lowest close since Feb 2, as foreigners sold about KRW 0.7tn of stock (seventh straight day, KRW 13.1tn in total) while still buying index futures. Bonds tracked stocks intraday: the 10Y traded +3.4bp in the morning and closed +1.0bp, and the won firmed 9.5 to 1,347.1 per dollar on softer oil and a weaker dollar.
Futures: foreigners buy both, 3Y settles cheap

Foreigners bought 8,729 3Y and 4,557 10Y KTB futures while banks and securities firms sold; the 3Y fell 4 ticks to 103.81, the 10Y rose 2 ticks to 109.39 and the 30Y fell 50 ticks to 116.98. Against our basket fair values (3Y 103.90, 10Y 109.38, 30Y 117.49) the 3Y settled 9 ticks cheap (about 3bp), the 10Y on fair value and the 30Y 51 ticks cheap (about 2.6bp), so futures leaned bearish at the front and ultra-long ends.
data: US nonfarm payrolls, October (Nov 6, after the KTB close)
Lifted December Fed hike odds to about 78%; US 10Y +2bp, behind today's KTB sell-off.
Record, first month above USD 60bn; supports the won and the BOK's hawkish lean, little KTB impact.
In line to a touch soft; the fuel price cap flatters headline, so it does not rule out a November 26 hike.
Strong end-user demand; the 30Y now trades about 9bp below the auction yield.
Trade strength underpins the won and the BOK's hawkish lean.
Fastest output gain since 2011; keeps hike pricing in the 1–2Y.
Large beat on chip capex and government spending; private consumption fell 0.2%.
view: The four-week picture is now more local than global: the 10Y is −32bp over four weeks, of which −14bp is US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.58 and −18bp is Korea's own equity-to-bond rotation, while today's +1bp was fully explained by Friday's Treasury move. The weekly rotation signal eased to +1.41 (daily +2.01) only because the four-week base rolled past mid-October; KOSPI has not stabilised, margin credit is 26% below its June peak and foreigners are still selling, so the bond-rally regime stays on. But the front end is fully priced for a November 26 hike to 3.25% and a 3.50% terminal (3Y 3.639%, 2s3s 1bp, CD at a 1-year high), so further gains have to come from the belly and long end and from Treasuries. I expect the 10Y to hold 3.78–3.95% into the BOK meeting, with US CPI on Nov 10 and the 10Y/30Y Treasury auctions the main swing factors; I still would not chase below 3.85% and would buy 3.95–4.00%. I stay flat the curve until KOSPI holds a rebound for a week. The signal's record remains better against Treasuries (hedged rally calls right 67% of the time and sell-off calls 69%, against 50% and 57% outright; Sharpe 1.30 vs 0.99), so a KTB 10Y long against about 0.6 × US 10Y is still the cleaner expression than outright duration, with the KTB–UST gap at its widest of the year the main cost.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 2.8bp to 3.629%, 61st percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.37%), and the 1Y 1.7bp to 3.568% (86th), so 1s2s is 6.1bp, still the 1st percentile (average 30bp), and 2s3s is 1.0bp, a 1-year low. MSB 91-day 3.176% (96th) and CD 3.36% (a 1-year high) price a November 26 hike and a 3.50% terminal, leaving little room either way.
buckets.call: Not triggered: the 2Y never closed below 3.60% (low 3.601% on Friday). Keep: fade a close below 3.60% (target 3.70%, stop 3.52%); add above 3.80%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 1.6bp to 22.4bp, 1st percentile of its 1-year range (average 40bp) and just 0.6bp above Thursday's low where our steepener from 29bp was stopped (−7.2bp). Today's bear flattening came from hike pricing at the front, not from stocks, and KOSPI failed to hold an intraday rebound.
buckets.call: Stay flat. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures) only once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; then target 30bp, stop 18bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.863% is at the 47th percentile of a 3.20–4.60% range (average 3.90%), −14.5bp month to date and −53bp since the rally call on Oct 8. Today's +1.0bp matched the 0.9bp implied by Friday's Treasury move; the KTB–UST gap of −99.7bp is a 1-year extreme, so an outright long has little cushion if US CPI or auctions push Treasuries higher.
buckets.call: Buy zone 3.95–4.00% not reached; keep it, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%. Don't chase below 3.85%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s narrowed 0.4bp to +2.5bp, still the 95th percentile (average −9.4bp), as the 50Y (+0.2bp) beat the 30Y (+0.6bp); the switch from +2.5bp is back to flat. The 10s20s30s fly is 12.0bp (71st). 30Y futures settled about 2.6bp cheap to fair, a soft ultra-long tone. On Friday's trades the 20-2 2049 bond (153 trades) was 2bp rich to the curve and the 19-6 2039 bond 7bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, flat.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (23 trades) puts the 3Y 22.6bp over KTB, +0.9bp today, 67th percentile (average 19bp), so the overweight from about 26bp is 3.4bp in favour. The 1Y fit is 35bp over (96th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 31bp (80th, average 24bp). KEXIM has only 4 trades and no update today (low confidence), and the 5Y fits are flat extrapolations, so ignore them.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, 3.4bp in favour.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (62-trade fit) is 42.8bp over the 1Y KTB, the 93rd percentile (average 31bp), and 36.6bp at 2Y (87th). CD rose 2bp to 3.36%, a 1-year high, and CP held at 3.83%, so CP–CD eased to 47bp (94th, average 28bp). IBK 1Y (24 trades) is 34bp over, 86th percentile.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y rose 1.9bp to 4.332%, 0.7bp less than the KTB, so the spread is 69bp (87th percentile, average 61bp); KEPCO 3Y at 44bp over sits just below its 1-year wide of 46bp (average 34bp) and BBB- minus AA- is 583bp (75th). Credit is holding, not cheapening further, but there is no forced selling to buy into.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

ktb:10.note: +1.0bp, all of it the UST move

watch: Next: US 3Y auction tonight (Nov 9), US October CPI and the 10Y auction on Nov 10 (CPI at 22:30 KST), the US Veterans Day bond holiday on Nov 11, Korea's November 1–10 exports around Nov 11, the US 30Y auction on Nov 12, the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), then the BOK meeting on Nov 26 and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; a hot US CPI or weak auctions would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.5bp per bp, while a KOSPI rebound with foreigners turning buyers is the local risk to the rally.
